text: One thing that worked for me is to realise you don't need perfect sleep for a good training session. Sleep is crucial for recovery of course but I was rationalising that if I only got 6 hours the night before there was no point going to the gym until I just decided I'm going anyway and I have had very few problems with consistency since. The essential idea is that if your brain is doing your best to rationalise that you're about to have a terrible training session because of x,y,z you're better off choosing to have that bad session (which might turn out to be a good one) than to let the lazy side of your mind win again. For most people having a sub-optimal gym session is still better than not going at all.

text: I think the key intersection between Motivation and Discipline is Momentum. Its harder to start a stationary object but once it is moving it takes significantly less energy to keep it moving. [...] Form good habits early. Really sore from the day before? That's fine. Don't skip your workout entirely. Instead go to the gym or track or pool to stretch or foam roll and ingrain that habit of getting out the door. [...] Each time you excuse yourself from a workout, slip on a diet, cut reps or sets, you are adding friction to your motion and making it easier to make those bad choices in the future. Motivation helps you gain Momentum. Momentum helps you form Discipline, Discipline in turn helps you maintain that good Momentum.
